title: fix(mcp): remove global request timeout
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Removes the generic 30-second abort timer from authenticated MCP requests.
- Preserves caller-provided transport/request cancellation through the native `signal` option.
- Removes the obsolete chat `timeoutMs` option and adds a cancellation regression to the existing smoke test.

Checks: MCP smoke test (3/3), Node syntax check, Biome.

gist.headline: Let the requests breathe
gist.blurb: The MCP client has stopped carrying a generic 30-second sand timer around. Long-running authenticated requests can finish their work, while callers still keep the cancel button.
gist.summary: Removed the generic 30-second abort timer from authenticated MCP requests, retired the chat timeoutMs option, and preserved caller-supplied cancellation via the native signal option.
gist.impact: MCP users can run authenticated requests beyond 30 seconds when needed, while transport and request cancellation remains available through AbortSignal.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli tending a cozy terminal garden where a long-running MCP request travels safely along a vine instead of being cut off by an oversized 30-second hourglass; a CRT monitor robot can hold a small, clearly labeled cancel lever to represent native AbortSignal cancellation. Include code-plants and soft glowing request packets to make the change feel like reliable, patient infrastructure.
